bullets.title: NVDA Earnings Tomorrow: Beat-and-Raise Expected; Options Pricing 4.6% Move
bullets.body: JPM notes buyside expects NVDA to report ~$94-95B quarter and guide $107-108B, with 75% gross margins expected to hold. UBS is raising estimates again ahead of FQ2:27 supported by Taiwan export data. NVDA trades at decade-low multiples with positioning score at maximum long (3/3); market throttling earnings reactions until Jackson Hole, with SPY pricing only 1/4pt for NVDA vs 1/2pt for Friday's event.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole Friday: PCE Tomorrow; Boston Fed Collins Signals Tightening Risk
bullets.body: PCE expected at 3.65% YoY vs 3.6% survey; Collins said tightening may be 'appropriate soon' if sustained inflation progress doesn't materialize, calling June/July data only 'mildly encouraging.' Jackson Hole pricing larger SPY move (1/2pt) than NVDA earnings, reflecting Fed policy as near-term market catalyst.

bullets.title: Global Inflation: Core Goods Firming, Services Cooling; Tech CPI at 4.3% Annualized
bullets.body: JPMorgan's July global inflation monitor shows core goods inflation accelerating to 1.3% annualized globally (strongest in three years) while core services moderated to 2.9% from 3.8%. Tech-related CPI picked up to 4.3% annualized. Baseline projects headline near 3% in 2H26 conditional on WTI easing to $83/bbl, but energy disinflationary impulse may be reversing.

bullets.title: US Macro Data Misses Pile Up: Consumer Confidence 7-Month Low, New Home Sales -10.5%
bullets.body: August Consumer Confidence fell to 89.4 vs 90.2 consensus (expectations component collapsed to 68.2 from 74.0), while July new home sales plunged 10.5% to 607K SAAR vs 620K estimate and median new home prices hit a 5-year low. Richmond Fed Manufacturing missed (+4 vs +7) and Philly Fed Services fell sharply to -10.6 from +7.4. Present situation component of confidence rose to 121.2, suggesting a split consumer picture.

bullets.title: Treasury Yields -5 to -8bp; Stellar 2Y Auction; Oil Down ~$2 on Hormuz De-escalation
bullets.body: 10-year yields fell 7.5bp to 4.629% and 2-year fell 5.3bp to 4.183% as oil (WTI) dropped ~$2 to $81.10 on Iran-Oman shipping lane framework news, US mine-clearance announcement, and Iran-Pakistan diplomatic progress. The $69B 2-year Treasury auction stopped through by 0.4bp — 4th consecutive stop-through — with foreign buying at highest since March 2025.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz Partial De-escalation: Oman-Iran Temporary Corridor Proposed; WH Denies Iran Talks
bullets.body: Trump announced US Navy removed all mines from Strait of Hormuz international waters; Oman and Iran announced a step-by-step framework for a temporary shipping corridor with joint mine clearance, though the White House stated no formal Iran talks are underway. Polymarket probability of normalized Hormuz traffic by year-end remains sub-30%.

bullets.title: Canada Retaliates with 15-50% Tariffs on $20B of US Goods, Effective September 8
bullets.body: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of 15-50% on approximately $20B of US products including steel (doubled to 50%), aluminum, motorcycles, appliances, and agricultural equipment, effective September 8. Canada sees little chance of resuming US negotiations before midterms. UBS cut 2026 Canada GDP forecast to 0.9%.

bullets.title: AI Trade Rebounds: Semis +1.4%, Equal-Weight Breadth Improving vs Mega-Cap
bullets.body: S&P 500 IT Index closed +1.0% with semis +1.4% as the AI trade bounced after prior week weakness. Equal-weight RSP up 7% vs SPX +1.8% since May signals broad rotation beyond mega-cap. JPM's tactically bullish barbell approach broadens from AI/Memory/Semis to Mag7/Software plus Financials/Energy/Metals cyclicals. QQQ remains 3.2% below prior week and 1% under its 50-DMA.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño Chip Claims Beat Nvidia Blackwell on Perf/Watt; Built with Broadcom
bullets.body: OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, a custom ASIC built with Broadcom, that it claims outperforms Nvidia's GB300/Blackwell on power efficiency, response speed, and total cost of ownership, and runs level with Rubin architecture. The chip was completed in just 16 months vs traditional 3-4 year timelines. Analysts note OpenAI may only adopt 25-35% of its compute via Jalapeño by 2028, and NVDA still needs to sell 10M chips to many customers next year, limiting near-term demand displacement risk.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI CapEx to Exceed $1T Next Year; Memory to Hit 68% of CSP CapEx
bullets.body: TrendForce forecasts memory will represent 68% of cloud service provider capex next year. Jefferies notes North America non-commenced hyperscaler leases reached 25.5 GW in Q2 2026 (+32% q/q, +346% y/y), with ~47% of future hyperscaler capacity planned as leased. SemiAnalysis notes OpenAI and Anthropic account for ~30% of incremental compute and could reach 40-50% next year, while total hyperscaler capex is projected to exceed $1 trillion annually.

bullets.title: Nuclear & Renewables Surge on Hyperscaler Power Demand; Data Center REIT Volume +78% YoY
bullets.body: Nuclear and clean energy names led gains: OKLO +11.5%, BE +6.6%, NNE +5.3%, SMR +8.4% on AI tools announcement. July CRE transaction volume jumped 78% y/y to $74.4B, with data centers comprising $33.8B (45% of total). Jefferies notes hyperscalers increasingly turning to third-party operators to secure power capacity amid permitting challenges.

bullets.title: Goldman Credit Warns on AI Financing Backstops; NVDA/AVGO CDS Widening
bullets.body: Goldman's Delta-1 desk flagged widening CDS on NVDA and AVGO as credit markets raise questions about AI financing backstops — concerns equity markets have not yet fully incorporated. Separately, Goldman warns the AI story is intact but credit is 'asking questions equities have overlooked.'

bullets.title: PCE Benchmark Revisions in September to Cut Core PCE ~30bps; Tariff Rate Rising
bullets.body: Macro team notes September PCE benchmark revisions will reduce Core PCE by ~30bps, narrowing CPI-PCE gap. Core CPI seen exiting 2026 at 2.3% vs Core PCE at 2.7%, well below Fed's 3.3% projection. A 7.5% China tariff add is expected before the September 24 Trump-Xi meeting, raising effective tariff rate from 7% to 10% and adding ~$7B/month in tariffs (~0.3% GDP).

bullets.title: Citi Credit Card Data: August Spending Recovery Underway; Electronics +4.9%, Off-Price +10.9%
bullets.body: Citi CC data shows August week 3 total spending +0.4% vs -0.9% in week 2. August MTD accelerating at -0.5% vs July -1.5%, with Electronics +4.9% (vs -3.0% July) and Off-Price Retailers surging +10.9% (vs -0.1% July). Athletic Footwear remains weakest at -15.5% MTD.

bullets.title: INTU AH -8.6% on FY27 Guidance Reset Below Consensus Despite Q4 Beat
bullets.body: Intuit beat Q4 with EPS $4.03 vs $3.58 consensus and revenue $4.35B vs $4.27B, but FY27 revenue guidance $23.28-23.51B came in below $23.70B consensus; TurboTax guided to $5.38-5.45B vs $5.49B consensus and Q1 operating income guide dropped sharply to $902-915M from $1.47B. Both Citi and UBS expect negative stock reaction. Effective August 1, SBC is no longer excluded from INTU's non-GAAP metrics.

bullets.title: AMD Upgraded to Strong Buy at Raymond James; MRVL Assumed Buy at Rosenblatt with $300 PT
bullets.body: Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy with PT raised to $641 from $565, citing agentic AI as CPU growth engine. Rosenblatt assumed MRVL at Buy with PT raised to $300 from $240; JPM notes MRVL custom AI ASIC business expected to more than double to $4B by F28 with GOOGL partnership ($20B p.a. implied). MRVL reports Thursday with implied move of 8.8% and positioning score of 1 (light).

bullets.title: Midterm Election Volatility Hedge Emerging; VIX Futures Nov Curve at 19.7
bullets.body: VIX futures rising from 17.4 in September to 19.7 in November as traders hedge midterm election volatility. A split Congress outcome appears to be consensus, which would redirect policy focus to executive action, fiscal battles, and AI regulation at state/federal level. Markets also watching September 24 Trump-Xi meeting for tech/tariff implications.

bullets.title: DKS Crashes 30.7% — Largest Single-Day Decline in Company History on Foot Locker Disaster
bullets.body: Dick's Sporting Goods Q2 missed EPS ($3.53 vs $3.76) and cut FY EPS guidance ~18% to $11-12 from $13.50-14.50 as Foot Locker comps went to -3.6% (vs +6.4% guidance in Q1) and FL is now expected to post a $40-80M operating loss in 2026. Hedgeye maintains short with $90 target (4-5x trough EBITDA) vs current ~7.5x. Athletic footwear facing deep promotional environment with lack of core innovation.

bullets.title: Apple Launches M6 (2nm) Mac Mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio; Evercore Raises PT to $365
bullets.body: Apple surprised with new Mac Mini featuring its first 2nm M6 chip with FP8 matrix support and M5 Ultra Mac Studio, with pricing from $899 (Mac Mini) and $2,499 (Mac Studio). Evercore ISI reiterates Outperform and raises PT to $365. Stock was -0.1% on the day, perhaps reflecting modest near-term revenue impact.

bullets.title: August Seasonal Dynamics: Low Volume, Choppy Action; Clean Trends Expected in September
bullets.body: Traders note August is historically the lowest-volume month with choppy price action; institutional traders return in September, typically improving market structure. Equal-weight indices (RSP, QQQE) holding above 50-DMAs better than cap-weighted versions, supporting a broadening narrative heading into fall.
